name: Treaty with the Choctaw, 1825 (Treaty of Washington City)
promises: Article 1: a line from 100 paces east of Fort Smith due south to Red River would be the permanent boundary between the United States and the Choctaws; the United States would move settlers east of it and prevent new settlement west of it.
Article 2: $6,000 a year forever, applied for twenty years to schools in the nation.
Article 3: $6,000 a year for sixteen years in place of the land sale fund of the 1820 treaty.
Article 7: Congress would not apportion Choctaw lands among families or bring them under United States law without the consent of the Choctaw Nation.
Article 9: an agent and a blacksmith for the Choctaws west of the Mississippi.

breaches.what: The Supreme Court held that in locating the line fixed as the permanent boundary of Arkansas by the Act of March 3, 1875, the government made a mistake that took 136,204 acres of Choctaw land into the public lands, valued by the Court of Claims at $68,102, and that this was a just and valid claim.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Choctaw Nation v. United States, 119 U.S. 1 (1886)

source.title: Choctaw Nation v. United States, 119 U.S. 1 (1886)

breaches.quote: the government made a mistake, whereby they embraced in the territory appropriated by the United States as part of the public lands

landTaken: The Supreme Court gives 136,204 acres (the fraction is unreadable in the scan) of Indian lands taken by the mistaken line.
compensation: The Supreme Court included $68,102 for this land in the Choctaw Nation's judgment. The Encyclopedia of Arkansas says a surveyor appointed in 1877 found the Choctaws were owed $175,049.57 at $1.25 an acre, and that in 1888 they were paid $68,102.00, or $0.50 an acre.
today: The Encyclopedia of Arkansas says the Choctaw line was at last settled at the erroneous 1825 Conway survey. No Indian Claims Commission ruling on the 1825 cession itself was found.

openQuestions: The Supreme Court ties the line to the 1855 treaty's first article and the Act of March 3, 1875 (18 Stat. 476); the line itself is the one this 1825 treaty made permanent. The 1875 Act was not opened.
The Choctaw Nation hosts the treaty text (choctawnation.com) but no Choctaw account of this boundary was found.
Whether the Indian Claims Commission valued the 1825 cession (Royce area 122) was not found; Choctaw Docket 249 concerns other matters.

plain.promised: A line east of Fort Smith running due south to Red River would be the permanent Choctaw boundary, with settlers kept east of it, plus yearly payments and schools.
plain.happened: The Supreme Court held in 1886 that the government's mistaken survey of that line took 136,204 acres of Choctaw land, valued at $68,102.
plain.today: The $68,102 was included in the Choctaw judgment; a historian reports it was paid in 1888. The mistaken line was kept as the boundary.
